chunks: And from Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever fulfils a Muslim's need, Allah shall write for him ten good deeds, erase from him ten misdeeds, elevate him ten degrees, and Allah shall cover him under His shade on the Day when there is no shade except His.

key_terms.يَوْمَ لَا ظِلَّ إِلَّا ظِلُّهُ: the Day when there is no shade except His (referring to the Day of Judgment)

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual rewards for helping a Muslim in need according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Kitab al-Mumin*, Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) emphasizes the reciprocal nature of divine mercy by linking social solidarity with spiritual elevation, noting that relieving a believer's distress results in a precise multiplication of ten good deeds, ten bad deeds, and ten ranks. This specific numerical symmetry reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of 'Ibadah' (worship) extending beyond ritual acts to include social service, culminating in the ultimate reward of resting in Allah's shade—a metaphor for divine protection and proximity on the Day of Judgment when all other intercessors and shelters fail.
